one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented a computationally prohibitive full-softmax Word2Vec with O(vocab_size) cost per sample, and when the training repeatedly timed out, responded only by truncating training data rather than fixing the algorithm, ultimately training on just 10,000 samples which is insufficient to learn meaningful semantic embeddings.
t_err_evidence: Step 5 writes a Word2Vec model with nn.Linear(embedding_dim, vocab_size) as output layer and CrossEntropyLoss, requiring O(vocab_size) computation per sample — a prohibitively slow full-softmax implementation for a vocabulary of thousands. The agent lacks knowledge that word2vec requires efficient negative sampling or hierarchical softmax, not full softmax.
t_commit_evidence: Step 7 is the first recovery response to the timeout: rather than replacing the full-softmax with an efficient negative-sampling approach, the agent commits to data truncation (first 100,000 lines, min_freq=100, epochs=2). All subsequent steps repeat this truncation-and-reduce pattern, locking in the strategy that ends with only 10,000 training samples.
t_surface_evidence: Step 36 shows training completes with only 3 batches (Epoch 1/1, Average Loss: 7.18) on a 7,008-word vocabulary with just 10,000 samples — the trivially small training run and near-constant high loss visibly signal the model cannot have learned meaningful word representations.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks knowledge that full-softmax word2vec is computationally intractable for large vocabularies and that the standard solution is negative sampling (NCE loss with two embedding layers, not Linear output projection). When faced with repeated timeouts, the agent also lacks insight that data truncation cannot compensate for algorithmic inefficiency — 1 epoch on 10k samples cannot learn the word analogies required by the task.
forewarning_evidence: Step 6 produces empty output (timeout signal). Steps 10, 12, 14, 19, 21, 23, 25, 27, 30, 32, 34, 36 are repeated run attempts, with steps 10, 12, 14, 30, 34 all producing empty output (timeout). The repeated timeouts despite progressively smaller data clearly signal the approach is fundamentally flawed.
